approval: PENDING — the only open leg of the gate.

goals.text: A delivery team with no platform context can discover what the platform offers and what consuming it commits them to, without a ticket. *(PRD O-1)*
The availability a team will *actually* receive — the composite down the dependency chain — is computed, shown, and explained service by service. *(PRD O-2, O-3)*
Ordered prerequisites are derived from the catalogue, and circular dependencies in the platform's own documentation are caught at build time rather than shipped. *(PRD O-4)*
Eligibility by data classification and compliance tier is explicit, naming the specific control a team fails. *(PRD O-5)*
A GA service resting on a deprecated dependency is surfaced with its migration path at the point of consumption. *(PRD O-6)*
A team leaves with a concrete onboarding plan: ordered steps, approvers, elapsed-time estimate. *(PRD O-7)*
Illustrative content can be swapped for real data by editing JSON only. *(PRD O-8)*
The computation is a standalone, regression-tested library. *(PRD O-9)*
The portal is a deliberately designed product, not a default template. *(PRD O-10)*

scopeIn: `src/lib/**` — the pure logic library: types, dependency graph resolution with cycle detection, composite availability with working, eligibility partitioning, lifecycle findings, onboarding plan generation, shared test fixtures, and a DOM-free public entry point. *(PRD S-1, S-8)*

`catalogue/**` and `scripts/validate-catalogue.ts` — `schema.json` (including the eligibility vocabularies as enums), one illustrative service file per service, and the build-time validator; plus `scripts/check-bundle.ts`, the NFR-3 bundle-budget check. *(PRD S-3, S-4)*

`src/ui/**`, `src/styles/**`, `src/main.ts`, `index.html` — the designed front end: design tokens, layout shell, hash router, catalogue browse with filter, service detail with composite working, team-profile eligibility marking, lifecycle findings, onboarding plan view, glossary, illustrative-content notice. *(PRD S-2, S-6, S-7)*

`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig*.json`, `README.md`, `.github/workflows/**` — build, test-harness split, coverage, validation wiring, the Node `engines` pin, GitHub Pages base path, the Pages deployment workflow file, and the repo README. *(PRD S-5)*
scopeOut: Any backend, SSR, or runtime network call. *(PRD S-9)*
Real platform data or any claim about a real environment. *(PRD S-10)*
Full-text search and any index build step. *(PRD S-11)*
Cost and chargeback data or display. *(PRD S-12; ADR-0003)*
Automated staleness enforcement of catalogue entries. *(PRD S-13)*

**Executing** a deployment: pushing to any remote or running the Pages workflow. The workflow *file* is in scope (PBI-012); running it is deferred to the brief author — a recorded narrowing of PRD S-5, see ledger row 23.

A service worker. An offline **reload** is not supported in v1; only in-session navigation after first load is. This narrows PRD S-5 and C-1 ("full functionality offline after first load"), not merely AC-26 — see ledger rows 24 and 27.
